newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Japan shoe maker to reach profit target.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Japan shoe maker to reach profit target.

text.p: Japanese shoe maker Himiko Co Ltd says it will be able to achieve its sales and profit target for this business year, buoyed by double-digit sales growth since April.

"I believe we can achieve our target of 7.4 billion yen in annual sales and 1.4 billion yen in parent current profit (for the year ending in March 1998), as sales are rising steadily," Himiko president Osamu Shibata said in a recent interview.

Despite a rise in Japan's sales tax in April which has dampened overall consumption, the company's sales grew 14.8 percent year-on-year in June, after a 34.2 percent rise in May and an 18.1 percent gain in April, Shibata said.
Himiko has not been affected by the tax increase, unlike other players in the industry, partly because of its strategy of targeting young women who have more disposable income, he said.
"We target women in their late teens and twenties, and we specialise in products that are in vogue," he added.
Himiko, which initially marketed its products under several brand names, has begun to cut down on brand names, aiming to eventually operate under a single brand, he said.
"Sales increased an average 30 percent as a result of the move. We intend to do business European-style, where a single brand accounts for high value-added products," he said.
Asked about plans to open new outlets, Shibata said he expects to add 16 new shops to the current 144 outlets during the current business year. The company has no outlets overseas.
"In the long run, our goal is to expand into other areas in the country and achieve 30 billion yen in (yearly) sales," Shibata added. -- Koichi Kawaguchi/Tokyo Equity Desk (81-3-3432-9991)
